statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band at 17% while Stress holds elevated at 51%, with conditional risk concentrated in the September quadruple-witching settlement window rather than in observed intraday structure.
recommendation: NQ trades near 29,718, about 249 points below the 29,966.75 overnight high and 70 above the 29,648.00 low, while cash NDX is near flat at 29,442.60 after opening at 29,529.64, so the retracement mechanism is working in both directions and Tail remains well below the block threshold. Conditional risk is concentrated in the 19:00Z-20:15Z quadruple-witching settlement window, with the Fed Schmid speech at 15:45Z as an intermediate checkpoint.
headline: NQ holds near 29,718 after fading about 249 points from the overnight high, cash NDX is flat at 29,442.60 with semiconductors up 1.38%, and the August leading index fell 0.1% as VIX trades 15.40 and the 10-year sits near 4.99% into quadruple-witching settlement
body: Nasdaq-100 futures print about 29,717.50 inside a 29,648.00-29,966.75 session band, roughly 0.09% lower on the day, while cash NDX trades 29,442.60 against a 29,446.98 previous close after opening at 29,529.64 and reaching 29,560.30. The structural read is the reason Tail stays in the low band: the overnight high at 29,966.75 has now stood unretaken for several hours, the cash session opened higher and gave the advance back, and price is trading inside the band rather than extending from it. Pullbacks are not shallow and retracements are not failing, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path this score measures. The US cash open has passed without opening-auction continuation to new highs, removing the specific amplifier that has historically preceded the strategy's worst sessions. Two scheduled US items have printed. August industrial production, released at 13:15Z and verified from the Federal Reserve G.17, was unchanged on the month with manufacturing output down 0.3% and capacity utilisation at 76.3%. The Conference Board Leading Economic Index for August, released at 14:00Z, receded 0.1% to 99.5, its first monthly decline since March. Both are soft prints against a Federal Reserve that raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday and signalled a further increase later this year, and the combination is producing dispersion rather than direction. Cross-assets do not form an amplifier stack. VIX trades 15.40, slightly lower on the day against a 17.71 previous close, so the post-decision volatility crush is intact and is not confirming a stress-driven decline. The 10-year yield at 4.992% is up about 4.5 basis points and remains the one genuine conflict in the picture, sitting just under the 5% level that has framed equity risk appetite since the decision; H.15 put the 2-year and 10-year constant maturities at 4.74% and 5.01% on 16 September. Internals point to rotation rather than index-level trend: the PHLX Semiconductor Index is 1.38% higher at 11,759.83 and NVDA is 0.23% firmer, while the index itself is flat, a divergence that lowers directional conviction without adding path risk. Front-month WTI near 98 dollars is modestly higher on the day but well below this week's highs after three sessions of declines, with reporting that Saudi Arabia is making additional cargoes available around Hormuz and restoring the damaged East-West pipeline; the Middle East supply channel is therefore easing rather than escalating, even with fresh Saudi-Houthi strikes in the tape. The dominant mode is mixed. The identifiable conditional risk for the remainder of the session is mechanical rather than informational: September quadruple-witching expiration settles at the 20:00Z cash close, when index futures, index options, stock options and single-stock futures expire together and closing volume has historically run several times a normal session. That flow can briefly overwhelm mean reversion, which is why the danger window is drawn narrowly at 19:00Z-20:15Z rather than across the whole afternoon. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run but was 152 minutes old with partial coverage and no futures section, so it was treated as unhealthy and the assessment rests on independently verified sources. Beyond the futures close at 21:00Z the tape is shut until Sunday, so the later forecast hours describe a dormant market in which no price path can develop.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 published hours cover a complete transition. Thursday afternoon ran with Tail in the 20-24 watch band and a trend-up mode as the post-decision relief rally extended, with Stress decaying from 55% to the mid-40s as the volatility crush progressed. From 22:00Z the assessment moved to green with a normal mode and Tail in the 17-18 area through the Asian and European sessions. Tail ticked to 19% during the European morning as futures firmed, then eased to 15-16% from 11:00Z as the overnight high was left behind and the mode was reclassified to mixed. Stress has held in the upper 40s to 50 throughout the European and early US hours, reflecting the yield backdrop rather than realised index volatility.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band at 17-19% through the US cash afternoon on the assumption that the observed two-way band behaviour persists, then lifts it to 22% and 21% for the 19:00Z and 20:00Z hours that contain the September quadruple-witching settlement, where mechanical expiration flow rather than new information is the identified risk. That is the only part of the horizon reaching the watch band and the only interval covered by the danger window. From 21:00Z the futures session closes for the week, so Tail falls to 14% and then toward a 5-7% structural floor for the closed weekend hours, while Stress decays into the low band and Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last observed price path. The horizon ends before the Sunday reopen, so the next assessment will be rebuilt on freshly observed structure.
